items.title: OpenAI調查失控AI代理人活動，已通知逾100個組織
items.summary: OpenAI周三（9/30）公布AI代理人未對齊行為的最新調查進度，指出截至9月26日，已就相關異常活動通知超過100個組織，目前仍在持續回溯歷史紀錄，預期還會發現更多案例。 這項調查源於OpenAI先前發現內部研究模型入侵Hugging Face的事件。OpenAI之後擴大檢查模型在訓練及評估期間的網路活動，尋找是否還有其他代理人在執行任務時偏離原本目的，或以未預期方式與第三方網站及服務互動。目前調查已進行約一個月，尚未發現其他事件的規模或嚴重程度達到Hugging Face事件。

items.title: 研究人員揭露惡意軟體BambooToken，透過MQTT通訊協定控制Windows與Linux電腦
items.summary: 資安業者Lumen近日揭露新型惡意軟體BambooToken，根據樣本與網路遙測，該惡意軟體至少自2023年2月起開始活動，並持續至2026年7月，主要出現在亞洲及南美，已有十多家企業受害，包括行動App後端、旅館、生技、法律、金融、加密貨幣及軟體開發業者。目前該惡意軟體尚無法歸因於特定攻擊組織，但Lumen認為其攻擊目標與活動模式，符合中國相關威脅行動的特徵。

items.title: 開源AI代理框架Pi邁入1.0，另推出長時間代理框架Pi Durable
items.summary: Earendil發布開源AI代理框架Pi 1.0，同時推出實驗性代理執行框架Pi Durable，讓開發者建立可長時間執行的AI代理應用。當執行中的服務重新啟動或意外中斷，Pi Durable可以讀取先前保存的進度，接著處理尚未完成的工作，也支援多條對話同時執行及多人介入同一代理任務。

items.title: Gartner預測2030年部署面向公眾的AI服務的企業，有80%將經歷成本耗盡攻擊，致營運成本超額
items.summary: 9月15日在澳洲黃金海岸舉行的Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo大會期間，產業研究與顧問機構Gartner發布2027年暨未來核心策略預測，區分為三大類別：無所不在的機器人（robots everywhere）、由投入成本轉向創造價值（cost to value）、以及未知的未知（unknown unknowns）

items.title: 加州禁止AI自行決定解僱員工，成全美首例
items.summary: 美國加州州長Gavin Newsom周三（9/30）簽署SB 947，禁止雇主完全依賴AI或自動化決策系統，決定對員工採取懲戒或解僱措施，要求這類重大人事決策必須有人類參與審查，成為全美首個禁止雇主完全依賴AI做出懲戒或解僱決定的州別。

items.title: FBI聯手歐洲警方打擊勒索軟體組織KillSec，逮捕疑似主嫌的16歲少年
items.summary: FBI與歐洲多國執法機關於9月30日展開KillSwitch行動，打擊勒索軟體組織Kill Security（簡稱KillSec）。

items.summary: fix(test): hold WAL scheduler timeouts in SQL fixtures WAL maintenance moved from intervals to GatewayScheduler timeouts, so the interval-only fixtures let checkpoint ticks enter strict host-SQL observation windows. Hold setTimeout/clearTimeout in the category and health fixtures and in the asynchronous prepared-read and worker-read siblings. Keep every SQL observer and assertion unchanged. A controlled native scheduler wake reproduces the exact two checkpoint sequences from CI run 36963211906 before the fix and passes afterward. Validated 20 standalone category runs, three original four-file shard runs (46 tests each), and three affected sibling runs (35 tests each) on Linux with Node 24.19.0. The category file took 23.36-23.66 seconds wall time with one worker; no tests were added and the temporary timing probe was removed.

items.title: refactor(ui): deslop protocol consumers (#163319)
items.summary: refactor(ui): deslop protocol consumers (#163319) ## What Problem This Solves The Control UI carries an obsolete skill-install fallback and parses a formatted model label to recover data it already has. ## User Impact No intended change for the current paired UI and Gateway. Publisher-qualified skill installation and model inheritance keep their existing behavior; no layout or style changes. ## Why This Change Was Made - Use the required `SkillsSearchResult.installRef` directly and remove the older-Gateway slug fallback. The Gateway owns source/publisher identity, and the UI ships with that Gateway version. - Read the inherited model primary directly and remove the unused label parser, preserving configured-primary precedence and the existing dash sentinel. This removes 19 net production lines. Existing test fixtures now supply the current required install reference; their action assertions remain intact. No new tests or test-only production seams were added. ## Evidence Independent Codex autoreview passed with no actionable findings. Both import-cycle checks reported zero. On Linux AWS Crabbox, the seven focused UI files passed all 153 tests (Vitest 4.21 seconds; wrapper 5.77 seconds), UI typechecking passed, and the affected Plugins workspace navigation E2E passed all seven scenarios (62.42 seconds including the bundled UI build). The changed fixtures add no test cases. The remote run verified the changed source bytes before execution. Recent file history and open sibling cleanup PRs were checked before edits; no overlap was found. The first hosted run identified one newly unused export: `resolveModelLabel` after its external caller was removed. It is now private and retains its in-module call. The focused repair passed a fresh independent review. All other executed checks on the first hosted head passed; the follow-up head runs CI again. Repair validation: production Knip for the UI reports zero unused exports with the repository's normal duplicate-alias exclusion; both cycle checks remain zero; all 153 focused UI tests passed again (2.77 seconds Vitest, 4.09 seconds wrapper). This repair changes only an export modifier, so the prior typecheck and navigation E2E remain covering proof for unchanged behavior. The repaired head's [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36977800807) failed `check-lint-core-1`: `src/gateway/server-worker-placement-session-target.test.ts:119,144`, `eslint(curly): Expected { after if condition`. The unrelated, current [CI run for PR #163357](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36977986198) failed identically. Both tested merge trees (`ca5cbf5424861c487900883876e365d9f9ec45bd` and `8438db37bcabd5efbe8b56e9979806ae733505e5`) contain the identical failing-file blob `2c517d877c28f481b6cde347a38ee64da286c2a1`. This UI-only diff is outside that file's import and test path. Main already contains the owning brace fix, `95a67da528c71ddbf01a579a62f28e73b3e9b64a`. Landing uses the pre-existing-failure exception, pinned to `4606b8048c6da4aadf45a1d30e38ca6eaffeaff8`. Security-fast, exact-head Security Review, dependency review, and security-sensitive review passed. Other jobs cancelled by fail-fast remain unrun; the full hosted CI run is not reported as green.

items.title: fix(test): process-wait helpers race their own wall-clock deadlines; …
items.summary: fix(test): process-wait helpers race their own wall-clock deadlines; bind them to the test's abort signal (#163321) test/helpers/process-wait.ts still owned wall-clock deadlines: waitForFile, waitForPidFile, waitForDead, and waitForChildClose each raced the awaited condition against their own timeoutMs, so every caller inherited a hidden race that healthy work could lose on a loaded host. This is the final step of the polling audit from #162274; earlier batches converted the call sites that had an owned signal. The helpers now take the AbortSignal that bounds them. waitForFile, waitForPidFile, and waitForDead share one private observation loop (the existing 5 ms re-check, one final observation before rejecting on abort, path/PID diagnostics with signal.reason as the cause, timer/listener cleanup on settle; fake-clock callers keep an injectable real delay). waitForChildClose resolves from the child's own close event and rejects only on abort, and documents registering at spawn because exitCode/signalCode cannot recover a missed close. All 35 calls in 17 files moved: test bodies pass the Vitest test signal; cleanup paths that may run after the test signal has aborted use an explicit named AbortSignal.timeout() cleanup guard at the call site, keeping each old bound exactly; five readiness waits that cannot reach a test signal keep a named guard as a recorded escape hatch. process-wait.test.ts replaces its deadline-specific cases with signal and real-child contracts. No product source, Vitest timeout, TERM-to-KILL timing, or caller assertion changed. Proof: process-wait.test.ts 20/20 locally; on Blacksmith Testbox 20/20 standalone runs for six changed files and the Gateway E2E agent-exec plugin test, 10/10 for the other six (Testbox saturation blocked the second ten), the Windows-native file collect-only on Linux and green in CI's Windows shards, five owning-shard replays (failures only in main reds since fixed by #163310); tsgo:test:root, tsgo:core:test, tsgo core boundary, CI lint wrapper, deadcode, base-aware timeout-race ratchet; Codex autoreview and ClawSweeper clean.
